S&P Symphony w/ Leverage (101% RR/28.3% DD)
...
Daily, it rides S&P uptrends with leverage, steps aside when prices look “too hot,” and in downtrends either plays tech bounces, fades overextended rallies by shorting QQQ, or hides in Treasuries/short bonds/gold.
...
Each day it checks trend and “heat.” Trend: is SPY above its 200‑day average? Heat: RSI, a 0–100 gauge of how hot/cold recent moves are. In uptrends it holds 2x S&P (SSO) unless things look too hot, then it parks in SHV or briefly rotates to IEF/BSV/GLD. In downtrends it may buy oversold tech (TECL), fade sharp rallies with PSQ, go long QQQ, or hide in Treasuries/short bonds. One holding at a time.
...
Out-of-sample, this strategy targets ~58.8% annualized return vs ~25.2% for the S&P, with Calmar ~1.75 and Sharpe ~1.41, and a higher max drawdown (~33.6% vs ~18.8%). It pursues stronger growth with disciplined risk controls.
